source_title_hint: Fix Your TMJ Pain with This One Simple Exercise
primary_summary: The video explains that a side‑bent head can cause the mandible to sit lower on the same side, leading to a deviated jaw and bite asymmetry. Over time this weakens the lateral pterygoid (referred to as the lateral tear‑goid) muscle, limiting side‑to‑side and pro‑traction movements. A simple exercise using a rolled towel placed under the neck to gently separate the teeth and gently protract the lower jaw is presented to re‑activate the lateral pterygoid and improve jaw alignment and rotation.

classification.usefulness_reason: Provides clear biomechanical explanation and concrete exercise for TMJ alignment

problem_statements: Head side‑bend creates lower jaw position on the same side
Mandibular deviation leads to bite asymmetry and reduced rotation
Weak lateral pterygoid limits side‑to‑side and forward jaw movement
habits_or_contexts: Uneven bite when chewing or speaking
Feeling of jaw deviating to one side
key_visual_points: Jaw appears lower on side of head tilt
Lateral pterygoid identified as key weakened muscle
exercises_mentioned: Towel roll pro‑traction of lower jaw
advice_mentioned: Place a rolled towel under the most curved part of the neck so chin points upward
Allow teeth to separate gently then gently push lower jaw forward (pro‑traction)

knowledge_units.title: Jaw deviation caused by head side‑bend
knowledge_units.summary: A side‑bent head lowers the jaw on the same side, leaving the mandible behind in space and creating asymmetrical bite and reduced rotational freedom.
observable_signs: Jaw appears lower on one side
Difficulty achieving symmetric molar contact when biting
mechanisms: Head rotation biases the skull, pulling the jaw lower on the same side
Resulting mandibular misalignment alters bite and muscle activation
when_useful: Assessing patients with unilateral TMJ pain or bite asymmetry
when_not_useful: Cases where jaw deviation is due to dental pathology rather than postural factors

knowledge_units.title: Lateral pterygoid activation with towel roll (pro‑traction)
knowledge_units.summary: Use a rolled hand‑towel placed under the cervical curve to allow the chin to point upward, then gently separate the teeth and gently push the lower jaw forward to activate the lateral pterygoid and improve jaw alignment.
execution_steps: Place a rolled towel thick enough under the most curved part of the neck so the chin can passively point toward the ceiling (≈124.8 s)
Allow the upper and lower teeth to separate very gently (≈129.8 s)
While maintaining the gentle separation, gently push the bottom jaw forward a tiny amount – this is the pro‑traction movement (≈135.3 s)
cues: Keep the movement slow and gentle
Feel a light stretch in the side‑to‑side jaw muscles
Maintain head position; avoid excessive neck flexion
breathing_cues: Inhale to relax the neck and jaw
Exhale while gently protracting the lower jaw
errors_to_avoid: Forceful jaw thrust that causes pain
Tilting the head further away from neutral during the exercise
when_useful: Clients with unilateral jaw deviation or reduced forward jaw movement
when_not_useful: Acute TMJ inflammation or severe pain
